KNEE: Peak throughput 107.0 ops/s at clients=2 (p50=3.434ms p99=190.292ms p99.9=254.255ms).

KNEE: THROUGHPUT PLATEAUED: raising clients 2→8 changed throughput by -11.8% (within the 10% plateau band) while p99 latency went 190.292ms→361.798ms (p99 rose). Extra clients bought latency, not throughput — the saturation knee is at ~clients=2.
KNEE: At saturation (clients=2) the server used 1.01 cores across 1 busy thread(s); the busiest single thread ran at 0.99 of a core.

KNEE: VERDICT: reads hit a SINGLE-THREAD CEILING — one thread near-saturated (0.99 core) while the server's total core usage stayed at 1.01. Throughput is bounded by one engine thread, not by the machine's cores; this is the single-writer/single-engine-thread read path the off-thread reader pool (#336/#527) is meant to relieve.
KNEE: Server disk read IO at the top rung: 0.0 MiB over the rung (reads are largely served from the buffer pool when this stays low).
